assessment.whatTheyDo: Vocca builds AI voice agents that automate inbound/outbound phone calls for medical and dental practices — scheduling, reminders, intake, and common patient questions.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Company is dual-headquartered in New York and Paris, with a significant Paris engineering presence — roughly half the team and hiring is France-based, which could mean distributed/timezone-split collaboration even for a US hire.
Founders' backgrounds (Eliott Hoffenberg, Hugo Danet) are not clearly detailed in available press — no confirmed prior technical/founder pedigree beyond angel backing from Alan and Datadog founders.
Fast headcount scaling (40 to 80 by year-end) suggests the team will roughly double in a few months, which dilutes 'small team, high leverage' dynamics somewhat.
assessment.rationale: This is a real, shipping product with strong usage metrics (1,500 practices, 1M+ monthly patient interactions, 70-85% autonomous resolution, 10x volume growth) rather than a thin wrapper — it's applied AI in a concrete healthcare vertical with measurable ROI. The round size ($20M Series A, $25M total) is within the preferred band and investors (Norrsken VC, Heal Capital, Speedinvest, Firstminute) are credible healthtech/voice-AI focused funds, plus notable technical angels (Alan, Datadog founders). Docked some points for the NY/Paris split (partial geography penalty) and thin public evidence of founder technical depth or senior/staff-specific engineering openings.
assessment.summary: Vocca is a ~2-year-old healthcare voice-AI startup (founded July 2024) that just raised a $20M Series A led by Norrsken VC to expand its AI phone-answering product for medical and dental practices. It has real, growing usage (15,000 practitioners, 1,500 practices, millions of calls handled) and is actively hiring engineers in New York and Paris.
assessment.product: AI voice agents that answer and place calls for healthcare practices — appointment scheduling, cancellations, reminders, and patient Q&A — integrating with practice management and EHR systems, deployed across 20+ medical specialties.
assessment.team: Co-founded by Eliott Hoffenberg (CEO) and Hugo Danet in July 2024; ~40 employees across New York and Paris today, hiring toward ~80 by end of 2026. Specific founder technical/engineering backgrounds were not confirmed in available sources.
assessment.funding: $20M Series A announced October 6, 2026, led by Norrsken VC, with Heal Capital, Speedinvest, and Firstminute Capital participating; angel investors include founders of Alan and Datadog. Total raised to date: $25M (including a prior ~$5.5M round).
openRoles: Founding AI Deployment Lead - US Market
techStack: AI evaluation and observability tooling (per Senior AI Engineer posting)
redFlags: Public materials don't clearly establish deep technical founder pedigree (e.g., prior AI/infra company or research background).
greenFlags: Strong usage and growth metrics (2,000 → 15,000 practitioners in a year, 10x conversation volume, 7x revenue growth) indicating a real, adopted product rather than hype.
Credible, vertical-focused investors and technical angel backers (Alan, Datadog founders).
Hiring senior-level engineering roles (Senior AI Engineer owning the full AI stack) rather than only junior or GTM roles.
Engineers appear close to product: the Senior AI Engineer role explicitly owns voice agents, conversational flows, evaluation, and observability end-to-end.

name: VoltR
evidence: Headline: French startup VoltR secures €22 million to scale lithium battery remanufacturing in Europe

Summary: VoltR, a French manufacturer of eco-designed lithium batteries, has secured €22 million to accelerate its industrialisation. This financing combines a €16 million equity investment and €6 million in grants secured through the “Première Usine” programme. The equity investment was raised from the SPI 2 Fund, managed on behalf of the French government by Bpifrance as […] The post French startup VoltR…

assessment.whatTheyDo: VoltR is a French industrial manufacturer that remanufactures and refurbishes second-life lithium-ion batteries for e-mobility, electronics, and energy storage applications.
concerns: Headquartered in France (Verrières-en-Anjou, near Angers) with a physical factory — relocation/visa/time-zone barrier for a US-based candidate, and no evidence of US-based or remote hiring
Core business is battery remanufacturing/industrial hardware operations, not software, AI, or any of the candidate's listed interest themes
No evidence of senior/staff software or product engineering roles; this looks like a manufacturing operation where software would be a small support function at best
Could not find founders' technical backgrounds or named investors beyond Bpifrance and Decathlon Pulse funds
assessment.rationale: VoltR is a real, revenue-generating industrial company (named clients, a factory, staged funding from €4M to €22M) rather than a shell or fund, but it is a battery remanufacturing manufacturer in France with no visible software/product engineering core — it matches none of the candidate's interest themes and sits outside their preferred US geography, making it a poor fit for someone evaluating places to join as a software engineer or PM.
assessment.summary: VoltR is a French cleantech/industrial startup that remanufactures lithium-ion batteries (second-life cells) for mobility, electronics, and energy storage, recently raising €22M (€16M equity + €6M grants) to scale its factory in Anjou, France. It's a legitimate operating manufacturer with real clients (Lime, Leroy Merlin, Decathlon-adjacent), but there's no indication it's a software- or product-engineering-driven company, and it's based in France, not the US.
assessment.product: Remanufactured/refurbished lithium-ion batteries and battery health diagnostics (SOH testing), collection, and repair services for e-mobility, electronics, and energy storage customers.
assessment.team: Founded in 2022; CEO identified as Maxime Bleskine, with co-founders including Alban Regnier, François Mallet, and Thibaud Maufront per press/aggregator sources (not independently confirmed on their own site). No technical/engineering backgrounds for the founders were found.
assessment.funding: €4 million raised in April 2024; €22 million secured around October 2026 (€16M equity from the SPI 2 Fund managed by Bpifrance, plus €6M in grants via the 'Première Usine' program); press also references Decathlon Pulse as a backer.
redFlags: Non-US headquarters with a physical factory, making remote/onsite joining difficult for a US-based engineer
No visible engineering or product job postings; careers page exists on Welcome to the Jungle but no specific roles were listed
Business is industrial manufacturing/remanufacturing, not software-centric — low likelihood of the 'engineers close to product decisions' dynamic the candidate wants
greenFlags: Real, shipped product with named commercial clients (Lime, Leroy Merlin, Moma Bikes, Decathlon-adjacent)
Staged funding growth (€4M → €22M) with grant-backed industrialization, suggesting real traction rather than hype
